title: Boundary cube attachment for coherent rigidification
statement:
Use small simplicial categories and their colimits and the two-object category $U(K)$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting], and the subset-poset coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], in fixed universes enlarged when necessary. For $m\geq0$ put $B_m=(\Delta^1)^m$ and let $\partial B_m$ be the union of its coordinate faces $t_j=0$ and $t_j=1$; by convention $B_0=\Delta^0$ and $\partial B_0=\varnothing$. For every $n\geq1$, the canonical functor $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]\to\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ is injective on objects and mapping simplicial sets. Both object sets are $\{0,\ldots,n\}$. All mapping simplicial sets agree except the one from $0$ to $n$, where the functor is the inclusion $\partial B_{n-1}\hookrightarrow B_{n-1}$ under the characteristic-function identification of the subset poset with the cube. More precisely, the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}U(\partial B_{n-1})&\longrightarrow&\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ U(B_{n-1})&\longrightarrow&\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\end{array}$$
is a pushout of simplicial categories, where the two objects of $U$ go to $0,n$ and the horizontal maps on their forward mapping simplicial sets are the displayed identifications. For $n=0$ the boundary functor is $\varnothing\to\{0\}$. No local Kan or model-structure hypothesis on a target category is required.

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, first paragraph and the two following bullets; printed p. 90 (PDF p. 107, zero indexed). No Stacks tag states this calculation. Online text read; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Write $V=\{0,\ldots,n\}$ and initially suppose $n\geq1$. By [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], a degree-$q$ simplex of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n](i,j)$, for $i\leq j$, is a chain $S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_q\subseteq\{i,\ldots,j\}$ containing $i,j$ in every term; composition takes termwise unions. For $i=j$ there is just the identity chain, and for $i>j$ the mapping set is empty. For $i<j$, record membership of each interior vertex in each $S_r$. This gives a bijection, commuting with every simplicial operator, to the degree-$q$ simplices of $(\Delta^1)^{j-i-1}$: each coordinate is a nondecreasing $0$-$1$ sequence of length $q+1$, and the inverse inserts the two endpoints. In particular $(i,j)=(0,n)$ gives the asserted characteristic-function isomorphism with $B_{n-1}$.

proof.text:
Define a simplicial category $A$ with objects $V$ by taking the same mapping sets as $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$, except that $A(0,n)$ consists of the chains for which $S_q

Under Step 1 this is exactly $\partial B_{n-1}$: a coordinate is constantly $0$ precisely when its vertex is absent from $S_q$, and constantly $1$ precisely when its vertex belongs to $S_0$. This condition is closed under all simplicial operators. Composition is inherited union. The only closure to check is a composite from $0$ through $k$ to $n$, with $0<k<n$; its initial subset contains $k$, so lies in $A(0,n)$. For a composition with output $(0,n)$ through $k=0$ or $k=n$, one factor is an identity, so the unit law keeps the composite in $A(0,n)$. Thus $A$ is indeed a simplicial subcategory. Every proper nonempty subset $F\subsetneq V$ defines an ordered face $\Delta^F$ and an enriched functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^F]	o A$ by inclusions of subsets; if it has endpoints $0,n$, its chains have $S_q\subseteq F
e V$. These functors agree on inclusions of faces. Here we use exactly the mapping sets, union composition and monotone-image maps stated in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching].

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, boundary-description bullets; agent construction of the candidate boundary category

proof.text: We now verify the colimit, rather than assume that taking a colimit of enriched categories preserves mapping-set injections. A compatible cocone from the coherent realizations of proper nonempty faces to any simplicial category $D$ consists of functors $f_F:\mathfrak C[\Delta^F]\to D$ agreeing under inclusions. Such a cocone is equivalent to one over all simplices of $\partial\Delta^n$: each simplex factors uniquely as a surjection onto its image face followed by that face inclusion; apply the monotone-image functor of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] to define its cocone map. For a morphism of simplices, the corresponding image faces are nested and the factorizations compose, so these maps are compatible. Conversely restriction to the nondegenerate faces recovers the cocone. We construct its unique extension $f:A\to D$. Its object at $i$ is forced by the vertex face. For a chain $S_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq S_q$ from $i<j$, list $S_0=\{a_0=i<a_1<\cdots<a_r=j\}$, and set $T_b=S_q\cap[a_{b-1},a_b]$ for $1\leq b\leq r$. Each $T_b$ is a proper subset of $V$: if $r\geq2$ its interval misses an endpoint of $V$, whereas for $r=1$ the interval is proper unless $(i,j)=(0,n)$, in which case the definition of $A$ forces $S_q\ne V$. The restricted chains $S_t\cap[a_{b-1},a_b]$ therefore belong to $\mathfrak C[\Delta^{T_b}]$. Define $f$ on the original chain as the composite, in increasing $b$, of their images under $f_{T_b}$. On diagonal chains take the identities. This constructs a value on every mapping simplex without choosing an unrecorded lift.

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, boundary-description bullets; agent expansion of the colimit universal property

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-face-cocone-splitting-refinement] with $V=\{0,\ldots,n\}$, $\mathcal F$ the proper nonempty subsets, and the compatible cocone $f_F$ of Step 3. Since $n\geq1$, this family contains every singleton and is closed under nonempty subsets. The proper-support check in Step 3 makes the canonical splitting admissible. The cited lemma says that any admissible splitting gives the same evaluation, including after adding vertices of $S_0$. Thus the value constructed in Step 3 is unchanged by every refinement used below.

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, boundary-description bullets; agent proof of simplicial compatibility, composition and uniqueness

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-face-cocone-evaluation-simplicial] to the same family, cocone and admissible canonical splitting. For each $\alpha:[p]\to[q]$, its conclusion gives admissibility after the operator and the equality $f(\alpha^*S)=\alpha^*f(S)$. This includes the first face, even when $S_{\alpha(0)}$ is strictly larger than $S_0$, and all degeneracies. On diagonal mapping sets the assignment is the identity simplex at the chosen object and commutes with operators as well. Hence Step 3 defines simplicial maps on all mapping sets.

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, boundary-description bullets; agent proof of simplicial compatibility, composition and uniqueness

proof.text: For composable nonidentity chains $S:i\to j$ and $S':j\to k$, the canonical splitting of their termwise union is the concatenation of their canonical splittings at $j$; each restricted factor and its support is unchanged. The evaluation formula of Step 3 therefore preserves composition by associativity in $D$. Identities are preserved by construction. If a chain lies in a proper face $F$, all its restricted supports lie in $F$, so cocone compatibility evaluates its factors using $f_F$; their union is the original chain, and functoriality of $f_F$ gives $f(S)=f_F(S)$. These assertions use exactly union composition from [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Thus $f:A\to D$ extends the face cocone.

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, boundary-description bullets; agent proof of simplicial compatibility, composition and uniqueness

proof.text: Every chain in $A$ is the union composite of the restricted proper-face chains constructed in Step 3. Any functor extending the cocone must therefore take the value specified there; its object map is forced by the vertex faces. This proves uniqueness. Together with Steps 3–6 and the equivalence of face cocones and simplex cocones in Step 3, it gives the colimit universal property defining $\mathfrak C[\partial\Delta^n]$ in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching]. Its comparison with $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ is the subcategory inclusion of Step 2. Thus all objects and nonexceptional mapping sets agree, the exceptional map is $\partial B_{n-1}\hookrightarrow B_{n-1}$, and all maps are injective.

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, boundary-description bullets; agent proof of simplicial compatibility, composition and uniqueness

proof.text: Use $U(K)$ as explicitly defined in [lem-coef-simplicial-interval-lifting]. For any target $D$, a compatible pair consisting of a functor $g:A\to D$ and a functor $U(B_{n-1})\to D$ agreeing on $U(\partial B_{n-1})$ gives the same object choices at $0,n$, together with a simplicial map $h:B_{n-1}\to D(g0,gn)$ extending $g$ on the boundary. Define a functor $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]\to D$ to be $g$ on objects and on all nonexceptional mapping sets, and $h$ on $(0,n)$. The only nonidentity composition whose output is exceptional factors through some $0<k<n$; by union composition in [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching], its image has the $k$-coordinate constantly $1$, and therefore lies in $\partial B_{n-1}$, where $h=g$ and the composition equation holds. A composition having an exceptional input has only an identity as its other input, so the unit equation suffices. These checks hold in every simplicial degree and also when the object choices in $D$ coincide. The extension is unique on each mapping set. Conversely any functor out of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^n]$ restricts to just this compatible pair. This is the pushout universal property of the displayed square; the horizontal maps send the labels to $0,n$ and the forward mapping sets by Step 1's identifications.

source.place: HTT §2.2.5, proof of Theorem 2.2.5.1, sentence after the two bullets; agent verification against arbitrary target categories

proof.text: For $n=0$, the boundary has no simplices, so the colimit of [lem-coef-pinched-cube-latching] is the empty simplicial category: it has exactly one functor to every target. Its formula for $\mathfrak C[\Delta^0]$ gives one object with the identity mapping set $\Delta^0$. The boundary functor is thus $\varnothing\to\{0\}$. For $n=1$, the condition in Step 2 excludes the only chain from $0$ to $1$, so $A(0,1)=\varnothing=\partial B_0$, and Step 8 freely adds the unique vertex of $B_0$ as the single arrow. All constructions and universal properties above used arbitrary simplicial targets, so no local Kan or model-structure assumption was required.

lean.statement: theorem rigidification_boundary_cube (n : ℕ) : (n = 0 → IsEmpty (rigidification.obj (SSet.boundary 0) : Type u) ∧ Nonempty ((rigidification.obj Δ[0] : Type u) ≃ ULift.{u} PUnit) ∧ ∀ a b : (rigidification.obj Δ[0] : Type u), Nonempty (CoherentNerve.hom (rigidification.obj Δ[0]) a b ≅ Δ[0])) ∧ (0 < n → BoundaryCubeAttachmentData n)
lean.note: The cube is the finite product of standard 1-simplices and its boundary is the supremum of the coordinate preimages of the standard 1-simplex boundary. BoundaryCubeAttachmentData records the object bijections, object and mapping injectivity, isomorphisms on every nonexceptional mapping space, the exceptional boundary/cube comparison, and the enriched pushout with U. The theorem has the n=0 case (empty boundary realization; one-object realization of the point whose mapping simplicial set is Delta[0], i.e. the boundary functor is empty-to-{0}) and the n>0 attachment case, with no target fibrancy hypothesis. Reviewer fix: the n=0 clause now also states the mapping simplicial set of the one-object category.
